thesis: Eli Lilly is the dominant force in the incretin (GLP-1) era, with the tirzepatide franchise — Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for obesity — driving triple-digit growth and now joined by orforglipron, the first oral small-molecule GLP-1 approved for obesity. TTM revenue reached $72.25B (+47%) with net income of $25.28B (+128%) and EPS of $28.15, and the pipeline extends the lead with retatrutide (triple agonist, Q1 2027 filing after ~56 lbs average weight loss) and Kisunla in Alzheimer's. At ~$1,221 the stock trades near the ~$1,277 consensus (Buy) target at ~34x forward earnings — a premium multiple justified by category leadership, but exposed to Novo Nordisk competition and litigation, drug-pricing policy, and manufacturing execution.

drivers: Orforglipron ramps into a mass-market oral GLP-1, expanding the obesity/diabetes TAM well beyond the injectable-treated population and reaching global markets with lower cold-chain and manufacturing constraints
Tirzepatide franchise (Mounjaro + Zepbound) sustains high growth as capacity expands and label indications broaden (sleep apnea, cardiovascular, MASH)
Retatrutide (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist) delivers best-in-class ~20%+ weight loss, files Q1 2027, and becomes a multi-billion-dollar next-generation obesity drug
Kisunla (donanemab) and the oncology/immunology portfolio (Verzenio, Ebglyss, Taltz) diversify growth beyond incretins
Massive US and global manufacturing buildout relieves supply constraints and lets Lilly capture unmet obesity demand ahead of competitors

base_case.assumptions: The incretin franchise keeps compounding as capacity comes online and orforglipron scales the oral opportunity, revenue growth moderates from the ~47% TTM pace but stays well above pharma peers, and margins hold near best-in-class levels. The stock tracks the ~$1,277 analyst consensus toward the high-end (JPMorgan ~$1,400) as retatrutide data and orforglipron uptake de-risk the pipeline, while pricing pressure and Novo competition cap the multiple near ~34x forward earnings.

risks: Orforglipron obesity-pill sales disappoint (Goldman Sachs flagged a weak launch), undercutting the oral GLP-1 growth thesis
Novo Nordisk competition and litigation — including the injunction fight over Zepbound/Mounjaro advertising — pressures share and pricing
US drug-pricing policy, IRA negotiation, and tariff risk compress net prices and margins
Manufacturing/supply execution missteps or safety signals (e.g., GLP-1 side-effect headlines) dent demand
Multiple contraction from ~34x forward earnings if growth decelerates faster than expected (HSBC rates Reduce at $850)

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) run-rate, early orforglipron obesity launch signal, and full-year guidance update
Planned FDA filing for retatrutide following positive TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 Phase 3 results (~56 lbs average weight loss)
Orforglipron oral GLP-1 obesity launch ramp and additional label expansions across the tirzepatide franchise
Novo Nordisk litigation / injunction proceedings over weight-loss drug advertising

key_risks: Orforglipron oral obesity launch underperforms expectations
Novo Nordisk competition and advertising litigation / injunction risk
US drug-pricing policy, IRA negotiation, and pharmaceutical tariffs
Manufacturing and supply-chain execution across a rapid capacity buildout
Premium ~34x forward valuation leaves little room for a growth slowdown
